schools.name: Fistral Beach Surf School
schools.note: Open all year with beginner, improver and intermediate group lessons, bodyboard lessons, private sessions, a weekly kids' surf club and surf weekends. Lessons include kit, changing rooms, hot showers and secure storage.

schools.name: Quiksilver Surf School Newquay
schools.base: 9 Esplanade Road, Pentire, under 100m from South Fistral
schools.note: Runs beginner, improver and intermediate lessons on Fistral, plus private, children's and family lessons and Roxy women's surf weekends.

schools.name: Cornish Wave
schools.base: 40 Fore Street, Newquay; you get kitted out there and walk to the beach
schools.note: Teaches at Fistral or Towan, with the instructor choosing whichever has the better waves on the day. Group lessons (ages 8+, max 8 per group), private, couples and family lessons are offered.

schools.name: Surf Sanctuary
schools.base: The Headland Hotel, Headland Road, overlooking Fistral
schools.note: Family, group and bespoke surf lessons on Fistral, alongside SUP, coasteering and ocean confidence sessions. The school says it has no age limits or ability thresholds.

schools.name: Newquay Activity Centre
schools.note: Most lessons run at Great Western, but the team uses Fistral, a few minutes' walk away, when conditions or tides suit it better. Group lessons are 8+; private and family lessons from 3+.

schools.name: Cornwall Surfing Academy
schools.base: Holywell Bay Holiday Park (check the meeting point when you book)
schools.note: A family-friendly school that names Fistral and Holywell Bay as its beaches, with wetsuit and board included in lessons.

schools.name: English Surf School (ESF)
schools.base: Newquay; confirm the meeting point when booking
schools.note: Year-round lessons between Fistral and Newquay Bay, with a teenage surf club, surf camps and boot camp weekends, and heated changing rooms.

hire.name: Fistral Beach Surf School & Hire
hire.base: International Surfing Centre, north end of Fistral
hire.note: Hires foam and hard surfboards, bodyboards, paddleboards, wetsuits and neoprene accessories, with discounted hire if you want to stay in after a lesson.

hire.name: Quiksilver Surf School Newquay
hire.base: Esplanade Road, Pentire, by South Fistral
hire.note: Hires wetsuits, bodyboards and fins, SUPs, beginner boards in several sizes, mini mals, intermediate boards, shortboards and longboards.

hire.name: Surf Sanctuary
hire.note: Offers surf hire and SUP hire from its base at the hotel above the beach.

hire.name: English Surf School (ESF)
hire.note: Has its own hire centre with surfboards, bodyboards and wetsuits.

shops.name: Ann's Cottage
shops.note: A Cornish surf retailer with two shops at Fistral Beach, one of them focused on wetsuits and surf gear, plus a town-centre store. The range covers soft and hard surfboards, bodyboards, SUPs and summer, winter and spring/autumn wetsuits with boots, gloves and hoods.

shops.name: Sunset Surf
shops.note: Stocks foam boards, mini mals and longboards, bodyboards, wetsuits for adults and kids with boots, gloves and hoods, plus its own Cornish-printed clothing. Board and wetsuit hire is also listed, including winter wetsuits.

shops.name: Slide and Glide Surf
shops.note: Sells its own custom surfboards plus leashes, wax, ding repair kits and clothing, and offers surfboard and wetsuit hire. The site says new board stock is on the way, so ring ahead if you're after a specific board.

lessonsIntro: Fistral is Newquay's best-known surf beach and has several schools working on or right next to it. Beginners are taught at the gentler southern end, while the north end is left to experienced surfers.

text: Fistral faces west, so it picks up Atlantic swell more consistently than the town beaches and can get powerful. That makes where you learn important. Newquay Activity Centre describes the south end, sheltered by the Pentire headland, as the best spot for beginners and the area the surf schools use. The north end, in front of the International Surfing Centre, is a busy locals' peak with mainly right-handers and is not a place to learn.

RNLI lifeguards cover Fistral for much of the year, usually from spring to the end of October, from 10am to 6pm. Surfers should stay between the black and white flags, with swimmers and bodyboarders between the red and yellow. Rip currents are a real risk here: in July 2025 a flash rip opened inside the flagged area and lifeguards rescued 17 people. If the swell is big, book a lesson rather than heading out alone.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Beginners at the south end only
cards.text: The sheltered south end suits lessons; the north end and middle peaks are for confident, experienced surfers.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Mid to low tide, smaller swells
cards.text: The headland peaks work best around mid to low tide. A school will pick the session time and beach to suit the swell.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Rips, rocks and crowds
cards.text: Flash rips can form when sandbanks collapse, there are rocks and tide-cut rock pools at the south end, and the north end gets crowded when it's working.

hireIntro: You can hire boards and wetsuits right on Fistral from the surf centre at the north end, or from schools at Pentire and the Headland Hotel by the southern end.

text: For your first sessions, a big foam board is the right choice; the schools here hire soft boards in several sizes. Once you're catching green waves, a mini mal or intermediate board makes sense before moving to a shortboard. Sea temperatures off this coast range from about 9-10C in early March to 15-18C in August, so you'll want a decent wetsuit all year.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Foamie, then a mini mal
cards.text: Start on a soft-top; step up to a mini mal or intermediate board once you're riding unbroken waves.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 3/2 or 4/3 in summer, 5mm in winter
cards.text: A 4/3mm or 3/2mm with boots in summer, and a 5/4mm or 5/3mm with gloves, boots and a hood in late winter.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Bodyboards between the red and yellow flags
cards.text: Bodyboarding is popular but belongs in the red and yellow flagged zone; SUP hire is available from Fistral Beach Surf School and Surf Sanctuary.

shopsIntro: Fistral has its own surf shops in the beach complex, and Newquay town centre is a short walk away with several more.
shopsText: Ann's Cottage has two shops at Fistral itself, one focused on wetsuits and surf gear, so you can pick up wax, a leash or a new suit without leaving the beach. Walk into the town centre and Fore Street has Sunset Surf and Slide and Glide, both selling boards and wetsuits, plus Ann's Cottage's Central Square store.

lessons.q: Is Fistral good for complete beginners?
lessons.a: Yes, as long as you learn at the right end. The south end, sheltered by Pentire headland, is where the schools teach; the north end is for experienced surfers.

lessons.q: Where do Fistral surf lessons meet?
lessons.a: It depends on the school. Fistral Beach Surf School is in the International Surfing Centre on the beach, Quiksilver is on Esplanade Road by South Fistral, Surf Sanctuary is at the Headland Hotel, and Cornish Wave and Newquay Activity Centre meet in town on Fore Street.

lessons.q: How young can children start lessons at Fistral?
lessons.a: It varies. Cornish Wave and Newquay Activity Centre take ages 8+ in group lessons, Newquay Activity Centre's private and family lessons start at 3+, and Surf Sanctuary says it has no age limits. Check with the school when booking.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard on Fistral Beach?
hire.a: Yes. Fistral Beach Surf School & Hire in the International Surfing Centre hires foam and hard boards, bodyboards, SUPs and wetsuits, and Quiksilver hires a full range from Pentire.

hire.q: What wetsuit should I hire at Fistral?
hire.a: In summer a 3/2mm or 4/3mm with boots is usually enough. From late autumn to spring, ask for a 5mm suit with gloves, boots and a hood.

shops.q: Is there a surf shop on Fistral Beach?
shops.a: Yes. Ann's Cottage has two shops at Fistral, including one for wetsuits and surf gear. More surf shops are on Fore Street in Newquay town centre.
